text: Ah, the humble candle. A marvel of modern engineering, primarily composed of solidified animal fat or petroleum byproducts, expertly molded around a frayed string of cotton. It is the pinnacle of human innovation: a device designed to melt itself into a puddle of wax while emitting a faint, smoky scent that vaguely reminds you of a campfire you never actually had. We pay premium prices for this slow-burning tribute to entropy, lighting it to create an "ambiance" that is essentially just a small, controlled fire hazard in your living room. It burns down to nothing, leaving behind a tiny, useless wick and a sense of profound existential dread, perfectly mirroring the adult experience of spending your life savings on things that eventually disappear.
